plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 41: Atomic Structure
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.

elements: vertical z-axis line rising from and below the origin, with an arrowhead at top and the label 'z'
horizontal axis line through the origin extending to the right (unlabeled)
origin point where the two axes cross, positioned at the left of the frame
z-axis tick marks with labels from top to bottom: 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, (origin), −ħ, −2ħ, −3ħ
seven olive-green arrows of identical length fanning from the origin into the right half-plane (m = +3 at top down to m = −3 at bottom, m = 0 horizontal)
vector-over-arrow label 'L⃗' next to the topmost (m = +3) arrow
dashed circular arc of radius |L| centered at the origin passing through all seven arrow tips
dashed horizontal projection line from each arrow tip back to the z-axis at its m·ħ tick
four thin concentric angle arcs sweeping from the +z axis to the four upper arrows, labeled θ0 (innermost, opening to the horizontal arrow), θ1, θ2, θ3 (outermost, closing on the steepest arrow)

interactions.label: Magnetic quantum number m
interactions.teaches: Stepping through m highlights exactly one green vector while its dashed projection lands on the matching m·ħ tick, showing the z-component is quantized in units of ħ even though the vector length |L| stays fixed

interactions.label: Allowed orientations
interactions.teaches: Switching to the faint continuous fan reveals every classically possible polar angle, making clear that quantum mechanics permits only the discrete set of angles θ_m = arccos(m / sqrt(l(l+1))) rather than any orientation

interactions.label: Orbital quantum number l
interactions.teaches: Changing l simultaneously updates the common vector length |L| = sqrt(l(l+1))·ħ and the number of allowed projections (2l+1), revealing how angular-momentum magnitude and the set of allowed L_z = m·ħ values are linked

demo_steps.title: l = 3, all states
demo_steps.narration: For l = 3 the magnitude is |L| = sqrt(12)·ħ ≈ 3.46·ħ and there are 2l+1 = 7 allowed vectors, each tip on the dashed arc and each projection on an integer-ħ tick.

demo_steps.title: Highlight m = +2
demo_steps.narration: Selecting m = +2 dims the others and emphasizes one vector whose dashed line meets the z-axis exactly at 2ħ; the angle θ satisfies cos θ = 2 / sqrt(12).

demo_steps.title: Continuous fan
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the continuous fan overlays every possible orientation as faint lines, contrasting the smooth classical range with the seven bold quantized directions.

demo_steps.title: Lower l to 1
demo_steps.narration: At l = 1 the magnitude shrinks to sqrt(2)·ħ ≈ 1.41·ħ and only three vectors (m = −1, 0, +1) remain, showing fewer projection states for smaller angular momentum.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Pure 2D XY diagram (axis_screen_angles null). Use ħ = 1 world unit for tick spacing; z-axis vertical (world +Y) from about −3.6 to +3.6, horizontal axis along world +X from 0 to ~4. Origin at left of frame. For a given l, |L| = sqrt(l(l+1)) world units; arrow m has tip at (x, y) = (sqrt(L^2 − m^2), m) with m ∈ [−l, l], so the m=0 arrow is horizontal and longest in x, the |m|=l arrows are steepest. Dashed arc = circle radius |L| centered at origin spanning the fan (right half). Dashed projection lines run horizontally from each tip to (0, m). Angle arcs θ_m are concentric circles of increasing radius (e.g. 0.9, 1.3, 1.7, 2.1 for the four upper arrows) swept from the +Y axis clockwise to each upper arrow. Colors: arrows olive green #6f8f1f (highlighted one brighter #9cc41f, dimmed ones ~0.25 opacity), axes/ticks/labels black, dashed arc and projection lines grey #888888, angle arcs thin black. Default l=3 reproduces the source exactly (7 arrows, ticks ±3ħ).
interactionPlan.notes: Build each arrow as a custom group (cylinder/line shaft + cone head) so length and direction update on l and m changes; recompute tips from sqrt(l(l+1)−m^2). Use LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances() for the arc and projection lines. The continuous-fan mode draws ~60 faint green lines at evenly spaced polar angles from +z to −z at radius |L|, shown/hidden via the toggle rather than rebuilding. Angle-arc labels θ0..θ3 only render for the upper arrows and only when l >= 3 (otherwise show as many as exist). Keep all geometry in the XY plane; camera is a straight-on orthographic-style front view.

authoredContext:
The quantization of the polar angle for the l=3 state is shown in the figure. The orbital angular momentum vector lies somewhere on the surface of a cone with an opening angle θ relative to the z-axis (unless m=0, in which case θ=90° and the vector points are perpendicular to the z-axis).

The quantization of orbital angular momentum. Each vector lies on the surface of a cone with axis along the z-axis.

Seven vector, all of the same length L, are drawn at 7 different angles to the z axis. The z components of the vectors are indicated both by horizontal lines from the tip of the vector to the z axis and by labels on the z axis. For four of the vectors, the angle between the z axis and the vector is also labeled. The z component values are 3 h bar at angle theta sub three, 2 h bar at angle theta sub two, h bar at angle theta sub one, zero at angle theta sub zero, minus h bar, minus 2 h bar, and minus 3 h bar.

A detailed study of angular momentum reveals that we cannot know all three components simultaneously. In the previous section, the z-component of orbital angular momentum has definite values that depend on the quantum number m. This implies that we cannot know both x- and y-components of angular momentum, Lx and Ly, with certainty. As a result, the precise direction of the orbital angular momentum vector is unknown.
